content:
rachel: Heads up — enterprise customer ACCT-9128 reporting severe latency regressions (p95/p99) for /v1/chat since 04:07 UTC. They see many client retries. No surge in 5xx but high client-side timeouts.

tom: I'm pulling traces. p95 jumped from ~150ms -> ~1.4s, p99 up to ~4.2s in us-west-2. Top model is `redwood-xl-1`. CPU/GPU saturation on pool gpu-west-07 and a lot of small queues.

priya: I see an eviction storm in kv-cache: per-pool kv_cache_miss_rate climbed to 0.88. Batching efficiency dropped (avg batch size fell from 10 -> 3). Looks like a torrent of large-context requests (1k-6k tokens).

infra-bot: Autoscaler alert: scaling inhibited; pool `reserved-enterprise-west` is pinned by reservation "enterprise-resv-2025".

rachel: proposed immediate mitigations (fast):
  1) Apply short soft-throttle on offending API key to reduce burst—soft so we don't drop everything
  2) Trigger model fast-fallthrough: route key to compat smaller quantized model `redwood-xl-quant`
  3) Engage circuit-breaker on streaming and long-context endpoints (drop/queue reject above threshold)
  4) Warm one extra ondemand GPU in us-west-2 and allow temporary unpin of 30% reserved pool
  5) Add a `x-redwood-fallback` response header and notify account admin via webhook/email

tom: I can do (1) and (3) now. Priya, please handle (2) and (4). Support, prepare customer note.

priya: applying fallback rule via adminctl. payload: ```json
{
  "policy_name":"fast-fallthrough-ACCT-9128",
  "match":{"api_key":"ACCT-9128"},
  "actions":[
    {"type":"fallback","to_model":"redwood-xl-quant","when":{"queue_p95_ms":">300","for_s":60}},
    {"type":"circuit_break","route":"/v1/stream","latency_ms":1200}
  ],
  "response_headers":{"x-redwood-fallback":"true"}
}
```

priya: warming node: `infractl scale --region us-west-2 --pool gpu --add 1 --type ondemand` then `infractl warm --models redwood-xl-1,redwood-xl-quant`. ETA 3m. Also unpinning 30% of reserved pool temporarily: `autoscalerctl unpin --reservation enterprise-resv-2025 --percent 30 --ttl 15m`.

tom: applied soft throttle: `rbacctl throttle --key ACCT-9128 --rate 60rps --token-budget 300000 --mode soft` — starting to see queue length drop. Circuit-breaker enabled on long-context streaming route.

infra-bot: New node gpu-west-11 joined at 04:12:23 UTC; autoscaler event id: ev-1978001111-1.

priya: fallback live. adding a visible warning in account admin UI and sending header for telemetry.

rachel: metrics update: p95 reduced to ~280-320ms, p99 ~750-980ms. KV miss down to 0.42 after warmup and model quantized path. Customers still see slight degradation but no timeouts.

support: sent templated message to customer: "We've applied a temporary performance protection policy (soft throttle + fallback to a compatible quantized model) to stabilize latency. You may see slightly different output formatting; please let us know if high-fidelity is required and we can discuss reserved throughput." Ticket INC-9128 updated.

tom: notes for runbook: this pattern = single-key burst -> kv-cache eviction storm -> batching collapse -> sustained higher latency. Permanent guardrails we should add:
  - per-key rolling token budget with soft/hard modes (default by tier)
  - automatic fallback-to-compat-model when queue_p95>300ms for >60s
  - streaming circuit-breakers that trigger on consecutive slow requests (> N seconds)
  - per-key cache partitioning or sticky KV shards to reduce cross-tenant eviction storms
  - autoscaler "burst-override" ability on pinned pools with safety caps and audit logs
  - client-visible headers and account webhooks for any automated fallback/throttle

priya: I also propose an SLO guardrail matrix we add to runbook:
  - soft-rate-limits: free 10r/s, dev 50r/s, pro 150r/s, enterprise 500r/s (burst tokens allowed)
  - token-window: default rolling 1m token budget, enterprise configurable
  - fallback threshold: queue_p95 > 300ms sustained 60s -> trigger fallback; rollback when p95<200ms for 2m
  - circuit-breaker: 2 consecutive requests > 2s on streaming -> open for 30s with exponential backoff
  - regional_fallback policy: if local region queue_p95>400ms and data_residency ok -> route to nearest region with capacity

rachel: capture actionable post-incident items:
  - engineering (runtime): implement per-key cache partitions + smarter eviction (owner: priya)
  - infra: implement autoscaler burst-override + TTL-based unpinning (owner: tom)
  - product: consider enterprise burst-pack offering (owner: product_pm)
  - support: refine customer messaging + add webhooks for auto-events (owner: support)

priya: repro steps for staging and load generator (keep broad coverage of context lengths):
1) create staging key with enterprise quota pinned to reserved-pool-staging
2) run load generator that mixes small/huge contexts and racks up token usage for ~30-90s
3) assert kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.6 and observe batch size drop, p95/p99 degrading

Example quick bash generator (cpu-bound-ish):
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
URL=https://staging-api.redwood-inference/v1/chat
KEY=STAGE_ACCT_001
for i in $(seq 1 7000); do
  L=$(( (RANDOM % 6000) + 50 ))
  PAYLOAD=$(python3 - <<PY
import json
print(json.dumps({"model":"redwood-xl-1","input":"x"*%d}))
PY
$L)
  curl -s -X POST $URL -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$PAYLOAD" &
  if (( i % 250 == 0 )); then sleep 1; fi
done
wait
```

tom: CLI quick-ops snippets for oncall to include in runbook:
  - throttle: `rbacctl throttle --key <k> --rate <rps> --token-budget <tokens> --mode soft|hard`
  - apply-fallback: `adminctl policy apply --file fallback.json`
  - circuit-break: `adminctl circuit set --route <r> --max-latency-ms <n> --enable`
  - scale: `infractl scale --region <r> --pool gpu --add <n>`
  - unpin: `autoscalerctl unpin --reservation <name> --percent <n> --ttl <m>`

runbook-bot: Runbook draft created: "burst-eviction-mitigation-2026" -> https://docs.internal/runbooks/burst-eviction-mitigation-2026 (draft).

rachel: final operational notes:
  - add telemetry to billing so fallback events are recorded (for reconciliation and possible credits)
  - expose per-key p95/p99 on SLO dashboards to let account teams spot risky customers early
  - for enterprise customers, add opt-in dedicated cache partitions and reserved throughput offers

support: keeping ticket open for 48h for customer validation, closing thread when stable for 1h. thanks all :heart:
